itemTexts.description: A magical wrapping capable of binding up to five scrolls.
A magical wrapping capable of binding up to five scrolls.
A magical wrapping capable of binding up to five scrolls.
Sturdy shafts that fly straight and true.
A stout stick covered in pitch.
Paper of superior quality needed for the etchings of magical words.
What they lack in taste they more than make up for in nutrition.
A strong coil make of Hemp and Flax.
A highly polished plate of pure silver.
Heavy Iron spikes capable of being driven into the hardest of stone.
In combination with flame this becomes a poor man's fireball.
A fine wine distilled in the sunken city of Waterford
Well crafted armour worn by the legendary Karnak warrior Mordin, founder of the ill-fated town of Tre Mordin.
Given in thanks by the Knockerkin. A useful aid.
A small token given to the Selkies. It is somehow connected to the vile sea hag, Loireag.
Badge of honour representing the noble and proud house of Godolphin.
Note hidden by a Knocker hunter.
'The Answerer' in the old tongue. Manannan, Lord of the Sea, wielded this blade in his epic battle with the sea giants.
The 'Colloquoy of Ancients.' A book of Legend.
Chunk of odd metal found in some Gnoll caves.
A key found after a skirmish near Ryn.
An emblem worn by senior members of the enigmatic Silverband.
A precious stone given in thanks to the Knockers by their Selkies for their timely aid.
It is said that he who eats the Salmon of Knowledge learns many wondrous things.
A blade of impressive workmanship which seems designed for the purpose of dispatching reptilians.
Llawereint 'The Silver Handed', God of Rivers, created these for his wizard followers. Makes the wearer as supple and graceful as a winding river.
Tin miners employ these hats to light their way through tunnels while keeping both hands free.
Blessed by the unearthly power of the Third Rune. This shield grants superb protection to its owner.
Forged by Kynyaf to allow passage on the Runic ferry.
A gift from the frost giant deity Ymir to his devotees. Its special purpose is to destroy fire based creatures.
Cernunnos, the Horned One, wields this ancient horn to call the Wild Hunt to ride.
Fir'bolg relic supposedly linking the ancient Fir'bolg settlements.
Found in the Stronghold of the Seven.
A Tathlum is an ancient weapon. The head of a close blood relative of an enemy is taken and dipped in lime. Of devastating force when thrown only at that particular enemy.
Strange piece of twisted metal found northwest of the Runic City.
Found by Palthus on a distant campaign along the Runic empire's eastern frontier.
Mighty hammer used for tunnel excavation by tin miners. Also a handy weapon.
Teague had this helm designed to overcome his foes who employed sound based weaponry. Totally defeans the wearer.
Mighty spear of the long dead Fir'bolg hero, Cu Culainn, the Hound of the Host.
A lit candle made of human fat is required to cast the necromantic spell 'Summon Shade'.
Cerredwhen was a great healer who was blessed by this powerful relic for his good deeds by the God Dagda.
Gwyddno was a reckless but inventive Fir'bolg wizard. He crafted this ring to provide him with protection during his many long voyages.
Grappling hook found in the Praetor's private quarters in the prefecture of New Caster.
Magical thread. Perhaps something wondrous could be spun from it if the right loom were found?
Manannan, the Sealord, occassionally throws his hand into the fray by granting the use of powerful artifacts.
A giant sized barrel of rum. Strong enough to keep a frost giant warm in the fiercest of weather.
A shield imbued with the magical power of the legendery Ossian, Bard-Protector of the Tuatha de Danaan.
Wine of high quality
The bestial gnolls of the Grey Mountains in the frozen north are fine craftsmen of shields and armour.
Battle staff imbued with the dread power of the Grey God.
Orcs swear that their patron deity, Gruumsh, first handed this fell weapon to Murbad the Tainted to honour his destruction of the valley Sidhe.
A cavalry lance. A charging bonus is granted if on horseback. Otherwise acts like a polearm.
Standard issue to the elite fighting unit known as the Runic Dragonriders.
A mighty lance capable of delivering fiery destruction to its victims.
Worn by those corrupted by the Grey God.
A great songspell sung by Ossian the Lyrist. The cream of the Danaan warriors sacrificed their lives to allow Ossian to sing this songspell and prevent the Grey God's manifestation.
A long spear with wicked barbs along the shaft. It is designed to cause grievous wounds upon being ripped free from the flesh of the victim.
Brightly coloured trousers commonly worn by the men of Karnak.
Cernunnos, a creation of pure Chaos, uses this shield to aid him in his senseless slaughter of wild animals.
A vicious whip formed from the thorns of black roses.
Forged by the Shadow Dwarves of the demonic plane of Gehenna for their liege lords the Glooms.
An artifact created by an Alder Ent of the Boscawen Copse from his own wooden body. It commerorates the Battle of the Trees 'Cad Goddeu'.
A cruel corruption of the Druid's sickle used to trim undergrowth. The sickle is coated in a deadly poison form the sap of the Hemlock tree.
A savage weapon wielded to great effect by the mindless Deoc Garde.
A book of heresies depicting rites designed to summon a horrific entity referred to only as the 'The Nameless One'.
The battle standard of a Runic Legion boosts morale and empowers the Legionnaires who stand beneath it.
Mighiest weapon of the Tuatha de Danaan, a race of deadly archers. Arianhrod was a skilled ranger who was known to enjoy the kill more than her peers thought natural.
Founded of black steel in the forges of the Shadowguant's dark homeland. Wielded by the mighty Shadowgaunt champion known as the Executioner.
Ossian of the Danaan, reputed to be the greatest Bard in history, sang some of his life essence into this Torc prior to his final battle with the Shadowgaunt and their master.
Bathed in spells of ruin and madness - to peer upon its unholy image causes even the stoutest of heart to think only of flight and of imminent death.
In the hands of an Assassin this vicious blade grants powers of stealth and deadly grace. Rumoured to have been crafted by the Crocodile Dancers of Hupe.
Gremyr's personal weapon of choice.
Vicious blade employed by the Quicklings. In the hands of another, a dreadful curse.
Founded of black steel in the forges of the Shadowguant's dark homeland. Wielded by the Jedda of the Shadowgaunt himself.
This ring imparts much forbidden lore concerning the sluagh, an ancient term for the undead. Its possession aids in the destruction of these unnatural beings.
The Sword Archon is the fiercest nemesis of the demon. They are merciless in their destruction of these nether beings. This ring provides but a fraction of their power.
A malicious trap desiged by the fey Quicklings. Their motives remain impenetrable.
When first the Skalds of the northern fasts met the Bards of this land much musical lore was exchanged. Greatest perhaps of the Skald's gifts was the secret of this instrument.
Gorget and his band stormed Keep Brimstone and forced a truce upon the fire giants. These fire proof gloves were given unto Gorget by the giants in token of his prowess.
Vambrace was said to have taken a vow never to remove his plate armor until his quest was fulfilled. It became known as his second skin.
Semius, young son of the Praetor of New Caster.
Belief in the Eighth Rune is considered blasphemy in the Runic Empire. A persecuted cult of believers is thought to exist.
First used by Balor, a mighty Fororian King in his battles against the Boneshavers. Blessed by Domnu, the patron Goddess of the Fomors.
Guireterax. A stallion brought at great expense from the heart of the Runic Empire.
Grrrr...
A bag full of body parts found in a recently unearthed grave.
The essence of the lich Clur'can resides in this amulet.
Named in honour of the mighty Valkyrie Herfjuttor.
The Boar is the symbol of Independence. Teague wore this shield proudly in days of yore.
Pauldron, mighty Priest-Warrior of Arn, wielded this mighty mace in battles long forgotten.
Sabaton, Battle Mage of the Fir'bolg settlement of Murias, employed this shield to great acclaim in defence of his city.
Emblazoned with the symbol of the Runic Light Horse. Shield designed for use on horseback. Lighter and curved to allow the rider free movement.
Animating device used to control a Dweomer Golem. A useful defensive simulcram for mages to defend key positions against other spell-users.
'Druid's Knot' Made from sprigs  of the sacred trees of ash, oak and yew. Worn around the belt. The bonds of faith bind both ways.
'Druid's Fence' A cloak made from the leaves and bark of the sacred trees of ash, oak and yew. The bonds of faith bind both ways.
'Drink of Forgetfulness'
A ring to tie the wearer to another. Aids in the ability to resist charms and the attentions of others.
Shroud of swirling energy worn as a cloak. Capable of reflecting magic directed against the wearer.
Smeared with woad, a powdered paste which calls the attention of the Gods of War to the wearer.
Will summon a Urisk war party to your aid. Use sparingly, as it can be used but thrice.
Maybe the Quicklings aren't so bad after all ... to leave a gift behind in this way.

monsterDescriptions.text: Wolves native to the cold, northern mountains of the continent.
'Yrimthursar' in their own tongue meaning 'Sons of Ymir' their icy god. A giant race of humanoids native to the frozen north.
The Nordmen speak of a giant serpent that lives beneath the ice floes. It preys upon anything foolish enough to venture out onto the ice. The Nordmen are full of such fables.
Powerfully built beasts native to the frozen north. Often dwelling in caves in small families or packs they rarely seek trouble with others but will attack any who enter their caves.
A proud and rarely met denizen of the forests and plains. Totally unwilling to mix with humankind. As a result they are thought to be legend.
These minor demons live their often short brutal lives as servants to those more powerful than themselves.
Gibber travelled with Terksh into exile. A more cowardly and cruel specimen of trolldom is hard to imagine. He delights in torture and pain.
A Necromancer and Demonologist of considerable learning. Some say he is either hopelessly insane or possessed. He is rumoured to be in these parts.
Renowned hunter and mariner among the Nordman. Lives in the frozen north.
A mighty orc general. His implacable campaigns against the Runic invaders won him the respect of orcs and a huge bounty on his head from the Runics.
Kevardhu fights with his bare hands. He hates for anything to get between him and his screaming victim.
Nguthzg is a lava demon from the plane of Fire. He has been summoned against his will by the Demonologist Darvik and bound to his service. He appears to lead the Seven.
Guttur was the mightiest and cruelest of the Laerg enforcers. It is unclear why he left the Laerg homeland and took up with those not of his kind
A cunning soldier, Garanhir leads a company of Nordman mercenaries. He was probably lured down from the northern fasts with the hope of plunder and pillage.
Talk of the taverns is that Terksch was exiled from his native troll homeland for acts so despicable that even trolls wouldn't stomach them.
Mercenaries hailing from the rugged mountains to the north. A hardy and coarse race respecting martial ability above all else.
A high priest of the Grey God, whose name cannot be uttered. The true leader of the Seven, a fact known only to himself, Darvik, Nguthzg and now yourself.
Attack with a fierce shriek of ultra high sonic energy which can cause confusion.
Grey coloured arachnid of tremendous cunning and power.  Huge size and a poisonous bite combine to present a deadly creature.
Very aggressive and territorial spider. Often hunts in packs. Large but not very fast and thankfully not thought to have a venomous bite.
Large fat spiders that dwell in thick forests. Masters at using their environment to trap the unwary in webs. A bite that can cause paralysis.
Almost invisible against the backdrop of their native icy home, these large and aggressive nomads wander the snowy north in search of easy prey.
As beautiful as it is deadly, the fabled unicorn can make lightning fast attacks with its single horn, causing blindness if it strikes the eyes.
The females of this long forgotten race have mastered basic magic to complement their fierce physical attacks.
A mighty neanderthal being, distantly related to humankind. Powerfully muscled and armed with massive stone hammers and rocks.
'Stone Nest.' So named because of the enormous rocky lairs these monstrous wyms create along the sea cliffs.
Warped by the vile magics of Laerg shamans at the orders of their Dragon overlord, the Draco-Laerg is a mixed breed of Laerg and dragon.
Laerg domesticated beast. These walking reptiles are incredibly fast and have a venomous bite.
Laerg domesticated beast. An enormous reptile used as a shock troop. Few enemy lines can withstands its frantic charge.
The High Shaman is second in power only to the great Wyrm. He rules with an iron fist over the other shamen who in turn rule the Laerg.
The Laerg shamen draw upon the powers granted to them by their reptilian god.
Very little is known about this ancient reptilian race of cave dwellers.
It is said that young Laerg that manifest the correct tendencies towards size and aggression are streamed into a secret regimen. This is the result.
Dragons are perhaps the eldest of races.
Capable of breathing lightning.  Woe to the fool who finds themself in lonely company with one such as this.
It is whispered that these vicious wights are souls who have been caught in limbo, unable to proceed to an afterlife due to some curse or other intervention.
A foul spirit known to roam the scarred landscapes of ancient battlefields and other places of mass killings.
These magnificent beasts have roamed the forests of Karnak for as long as recorded history. Venerated by the locals, their image is often used on heraldic devices.
Not an overtly aggressive creature, the giant badger is however fiercely territorial and will attack without quarter anyone approaching its warren or young.
A snake of unbelievable size.  Easily  60 feet in length and as large around as a full-grown bull vusk.
A large striped and heavily furred cat with a mean temper and the fangs to back it up.
A large wolf whose very howl is said to cause fear. Probably just the excuse of fools who run when confronted with a dog in the shadows.
A large mountain cat with razor sharp jaws.
Many have heard tales of the Wild Hunt: of forests oddly depopulated; of an oddly compelling horn which sounds in the depths of forests far from civilization.
Malicious forest dwellers. They delight in torturing travellers with their cruel sense of humour.
A poisonous bite may be the least of your worries if you meet up with one of these vermin.
Knight-Marshal of the Danaan Riders. Blessed in the eyes of Macha, Goddess of Battle. Lost in the Great War a hundred years ago.
Rider of the Tuatha de Danaan. An ancient order of Sidhe knights sworn to protect the sacred forest shrine of Slieve Fuad. Now just a footnote in history.
Rumoured to be the sole surviving Rider of the Tuatha de Nanann. Changed his name to Cup Seeker (Per Dur in the old tongue) due to his hopeless quest.
Militia from the town of Pengelly.
Militia from the town of Pengelly.
Gwaf,  the Winter Dragon.
'Sword-bearer'. The Thane of Porthenys.
Petty footpads making nuisances of themselves in the low hills east of Porthenys.
Has risen to the questionable position of leading the Scum in their less than daring raids on unarmed merchants and civilians around Porthenys.
Smaller but with more cunning and guile than their larger cousins who they tend to manipulate.
Mean and ugly brutes that prefer to live in caves and murky swamps.
Considered a mighty hunter by Knockerkin standards.
A secretive mountain race. Very fast and agile. They are known for both their cunning traps and pelting unwanted intruders with relentless barrages of darts.
These blind subterranean river serpents have never seen the light of day. They hunt by following the water disturbances made by their prey.
A flightless dragon from the deepest depths of the earth. A true horror about which very little is known.
Young earth dragons. Probably best to dispatch them before they grow to full size.
A dangerous opponent that enjoys swooping down on its prey and mauling them with razor sharp hooves and a wicked beak.
River dwelling fey equines with manes of seaweed. From a distance they resemble horses, but they are ferocious flesh eaters.
Tales abound of these bizarre creatures. They spring from the forest floor to snare the unwary, utilising their near perfect camouflage.
These walking (or rather stumbling) dead are said to haunt the area where they met an untimely end.
Name says it all. They prefer to sneak up on their prey unawares, preferably with a poisoned blade. Cowardly backstabbers.
Men at arms for hire. Freebooters who turn coat to the highest bidder.
These guys rule the pits - too bad the place isn't worth anything.
The Avatar is protected by an aura of invulnerability.
Also known as Satyrs. Bestial men with the legs of fauns and small horns. Particularly aggressive during rutting season. Attack with punchs and a vicious head butt.
Well armed and trained mercenary in the employ of the Silverband.
Failed pirates who have turned to luring ships onto reefs to plunder them.
Town militia of Ryn. Light infantry, armed with spear and shield. Untested troops; who knows what would happen if they saw action.
Master strategist and former comrade-in-arms of Lord Godolphin. Present whereabouts unknown.
Cairbre, the eldest son of Lord Godolphin, is a celebrated warrior among the Karnak people.
Lord Godolphin has maintained control of his modest fiefdom through a combination of political cunning and martial skills.
Lightly armoured and hefting a vicious war axe, Karnak armsmen are not professional soldiers but rather ordinary townsfolk long used to defending their homesteads.
A cut above the typical Karnak armsman. These Karnak warriors inspire their troops through sheer courage and savagery.
Basic Runic troop armed with halberd and shield. Superb training and discipline has allowed Runic Legions to dominate the continent.
Runic squad leaders have been promoted from the lesser ranks. Loud mouthed bully-boys who keep the lower ranks in line.
Years of training at the Runic academy of martial arts combined with countless campaigns make this Runic warrior a deadly foe.
Light troops armed with sword and crossbow.
Prefects make up the Watch of a Runic city, keeping order through a judicious mix of diplomacy and heavy blunt instruments.
Raised from birth by the revered caste of dragon trainers these beasts are trained to be used as mounts by the feared Dragonriders.
A member of an elite force. Greatly respected among Runics. Universally feared.
This elite fighting unit represents two coordinated individuals. The Dragonrider is able to attack with his blade while the dragon employs it's claws, fangs and magic.
Light cavalry armed with sword and net. Drawn from the ranks of the non Rune-chosen. A bitter rivalry exists between the light and the heavy horse.
Heavily armed cavalry. Drawn from the ranks of the Rune-chosen. As deadly as they are arrogant.
Slaine is an accomplished captain of the Runic Heavy Horse. Popular with his own troops he is hated and feared by the other wings of the Runic army.
Light cavalry armed with sword and net. Drawn from the ranks of the non Rune-chosen. A bitter rivalry exists between the light and the heavy horse.
Former Runic veteran - now on the run.
So named because of the test of loyalty required of him to please his God. Flayt tracked down and killed his every known relative, children included.
Barnagh has travelled far from his native Calvert over the sea to the South, irresistably compelled by the drawing power of something beyond his comprehension.
It is rumoured that these are protectors given by evil deities to their disciples. Granted the dubious gift of unlife they serve whatever master they are given to.
High Prelate of the Gray God, whose name cannot be uttered.
As the wicked of the land gradually found themselves compelled to wander to Skullkeep, those with some martial ability joined the ranks of the Defenders. Fanatical warriors.
Whats the message?
A powerful dragon that tends to live in sandy areas. Its diet consists mostly of crabs and shellfish but it will happily eat adventurers. Thankfully it doesn't use magic.
An enormous snake-like creature that thankfully only lives very far underground. Some say its very gaze causes even the bravest to flee.
Yet another reason to lock the doors and gather by the fireplace in large groups. Avoid the moors at midnight if you value your sanity.
When the Runics scattered the Orcs and pacified the eastern regions several Orc clans refused to submit and hired themselves out as mercenaries.
An orc warrior of great martial ability. Generally a clan leader or champion.
When the Runics scattered the Orcs and pacified the eastern regions several Orc clans refused to submit and hired themselves out as mercenaries.
Also known as Hyena-men. Powerful semi-civilised humanoids with vulpine features. Tend to dwell in mountainous areas and live off raiding their neighbours.
A giant brute among Gnolls. Battle Chief of the Stone Fist Clan. Keeps his position by cracking the heads of those who would disagree with him.
Representative of the Gnoll Stone Fist clan of the Grey Mountains. His presence here does not bode well for peace in Karnak.
A mighty warrior of the Stone Fist clan of Gnolls.
Proud Sidhe warriors. Closely related to Grey Elves.
Skilled in the use of a bow.  These warriors prefer to pepper their enemies with fine yew wood shafts.
Skilled in the use of a bow.  These warriors prefer to pepper their enemies with fine yew wood shafts.
Karnak women fight alongside their men, matching them in prowess and often surpassing them in drinking ability.
Mischievous winged imps, these creatures tend to live in wells and crave shiny objects. Rumours of their granting wishes are greatly exaggerated.
This evil semi-vampiric race was thankfully wiped out at the hands of the Firbolg-Danaan alliance a hundred years ago.
'The Lord of the Mound.' A beast thought to be the physical manifestation of fey moor spirits.
Unnatural creatures spawned from the bowels of moors, fells and swamps.
Red Claws, also referred to as Blood Furs. Known for their bounding attacks: the beast leaps over its victim and attacks them from behind, causing entanglement.
Generations of breeding large mastiffs with wolves has resulted in a fearsome guard dog.
Crafted during the Battle of Mages in days long forgotten. Highly resistant to magic these slow but sturdy constructs animate at a predetermined trigger.
Selkie's in seal form are slow but have a powerful bite and layers of blubber make them impervious to cold.
Alder Ent of the Boscawen Copse. A race of long lived forest warders.
Magical experimentation with fungi resulted in this shambling creature.
The essence of anti-life.
An enormous crab with a carapace as thick as plate mail. Razor sharp pincers snap at those foolish enough to get within range of it. Only blunt weapons can crack its shell.
Also known as the Lyryon Gwragh, 'Flood Hag'. Banished from the Ocean for her cruelty. She is formed of living water. Only the sharpest blade will cut her tide.
An large crab with a carapace as thick as chain mail. Razor sharp pincers snap at those foolish enough to get within range of it. Only blunt weapons can crack its shell.
Cunning water spirits who take the form of fierce waves when threatened. They pummel their opponents with watery slaps as hard as stone and cold as death.
Also known as Sharkmen. These aggressive cold-blooded humanoids generally live in coastal waters or along rocky shorelines.
Also known as Sharkmen. These aggressive cold-blooded humanoids generally live in coastal waters or along rocky shorelines.
A demon lord who prefers to trap souls through cruel manipulation rather than brute force. Some demons mock his 'gentle' ways, but none can fault his success.
Raised through means never spoken of by the Druids. These thick necked  creatures exude a pungent smell and deliver punishing blows with their thorny fists.
Lesser Daemon from a plane of pure electrical energy.
Daemon from a plane of pure electrical energy.
Mantic overlord. A daemon of great cunning who has taken advantage of this opportunity to feed off the life essence of his mortal victims.
Former Prelate of the Grey God. Given the dubious gift of unlife by his Lord to continue his service following his demise at the hands of Diarmait Ua Duibne.
In life, a formerly valiant warrior. Now a walking nightmare.
'Full of Anger'.  The Nameless One's most devoted priests underwent a horrific transformation to serve Him in His next incarnation. They lie dormant until His summoning ...
Heroes from a bygone age, raised from death and enslaved.
Heroes from a bygone age, raised from death and enslaved.
Heroes from a bygone age, raised from death and enslaved.
A forsaken hero from a bygone age, raised from death and enslaved.
A bard of considerable talent. Known locally as a 'droll' the Karnak name for bards. Welcomed everywhere for their revered story telling abilities. Keepers of oral history.
A cut above the typical hired sword. Only the wealthiest of merchants are able to afford these solid mercenaries.
Followers of Baille, these misguided novices once studied under true druids until they were approached by Baille and convinced that his path was the one to tread.
'Tree wight'. In happier times, an Alder Ent of the Llengelly Copse. Now raised from death and enslaved.
It is unheard of for a druid to walk the dark paths and use his knowledge against the natural world. Sadly, Baille has walked far from the light of Arn toward the darkness.
Used by wizards to protect their belongings, the magically animated Gargoyle is enchanted to attack unless the correct word or gesture is given.
Finest of the Fir'bolg rangers. Gwydion is a valiant but reckless archer.
Noone has heard much of this deadly heroine in recent times. Rumoured to have taken up work for the Thane of Porthenys.
This Karnak brawler has been banned from almost every drinking establishment in the land. Buy him a drink and you will find out why.
'Razor Fish.' Large and aggressive fish. They employ a vicious bite to rip their prey to bloody ribbons.
'Bad Luck.' The local fishermen have long held that the mere sight of these monstrous fish brings terrible luck.
Generally docile and lethargic, these squat lizards give a nasty bite to anyone wandering too close to their lairs.
Forest dwelling toads, known for leaping from nearby trees to pounce upon victims and deliver a bite laden with corrosive juices.
Subterranean worms, so named because of their bright scales. A highly toxic poison is delivered from their powerful jaws.
Tiny, cobra like serpents whose venom strikes at the optic nerve.
'Evil ones.' These trolls rarely venture far from their cave homes, as most non-trolls will attack them on sight. Such is their reputation for cruelty.
'Dark Goblin.' Despite their name they are in fact smaller relatives of trolls. They often live in cooperation with their larger and stupider neighbours.
Huge claws and mandibles, designed for tunneling through rock, make quick work of opponents. Beware the eyes, which can cause confusion.
A dangerous opponent that enjoys swooping down on its prey and mauling them with razor sharp hooves and a wicked beak.
A demon who has failed to harvest a sufficient number of souls to enter the demon aristocracy. A foul and depraved killer.
Hideous demons, covered in wicked barbs, salivating corrosive bile from their revolting mouths. They are covered in weeping sores and dead peeling flesh.
'Dog Brother.' These large canine featured humanoids are said to dwell in the mountains to the east.
'Guardian.' Raised from the field of battle and given unlife, these shambling and disease-ridden creatures hunger for the living.
This ungainly but highly efficient killing machine has provided heavy artillery support to Runic campaigns throughout the continent.
'Watcher.'
'Protector.'
'Sword Hound.'
'Curse.'
'The Raven.'
'Marauder.'
'Growler.'
These vermin carry a deadly disease.  They breed so rapidly there are always plenty to take the place of those that perish.
End of List
End of List
End of List
